note: Adversarial review against the competitor PM angle completed.

findings.message: The plan relies on 'eager finalize on EVERY end path' to snapshot usage, explicitly dictating that a later reconcile 'never reads the prunable home store'. If the Anchor process suffers a hard crash (OOM, SIGKILL, power loss), the end path never executes and the snapshot is never taken. Since reconcile is forbidden from checking the home store, the usage is permanently orphaned and drops from the rollup. Competitor tools stream or securely recover telemetry from crashes. This directly violates the North Star mandate of 'measured truth, not zero-by-omission'.

findings.topic: JSON tearing on live heartbeat capture
findings.message: Wave 4 mandates taking a heartbeat snapshot piggybacked on the '120s autosave hook' and explicitly rules that a parse exception results in an atomic 'capture-failed' record. If the 120s heartbeat attempts to read the sidecar JSONL exactly while the engine is appending a new line, it will encounter a torn write, throw a parse exception, and permanently brand the active session as 'capture-failed'. Competitor telemetry tails active logs defensively; failing the entire session's cost capture on a concurrent read/write race is unacceptable.

The plan dictates 'no batch backfill job', relying exclusively on lazy generation upon the 'first open of a summary-less tile'. If an autonomous multi-agent wave spawns 50 one-shot jobs, the user must manually click 50 individual tiles just to trigger the summarization of what was accomplished. Competitor platforms auto-summarize wave outputs in the background. Hiding the 'what was accomplished' narrative behind manual per-tile clicks degrades the warm resume UX and obscures the project's state.
